clue.text: No stamp? He'll be upset

indicators.note: to be upset is to be knocked over, so the letters of the two words before are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A letter carrier is dismayed to find an envelope with no stamp on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be upset' rearranges NO STAMP; read as a whole, the clue also describes the man who would be bothered by an unstamped letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who delivers mail is the one inconvenienced when a letter arrives without postage.

clue.text: Occasional worker turns up to send carriage back

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means reading the following words from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to remit is to send, as money by post
a trap is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage

explanation.surface: A casual employee arrives to send a horse carriage back to its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses REMIT and TRAP together, giving PARTTIMER; 'to' and 'back' are linking words.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone employed for only some hours of the week works occasionally rather than full days.

clue.text: Sage embraces second wise man

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold within the arms, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: Solon was the lawgiver of ancient Athens, the proverbial sage
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A wise elder hugs a second wise elder.
explanation.walkthrough: MO, a short moment, sits inside SOLON, the Athenian lawmaker whose name stands for any sage.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical king of Israel is famed for his judgement, so his name is used for any very wise person.

clue.text: King and Queen as traders?

parts.note: on a chessboard these two pieces stand on the central squares of the back row, so they are the central chess pieces, punning on dealers between producer and buyer

explanation.surface: Royalty imagined running a business.
explanation.walkthrough: Chess pieces are called men, and the king and queen occupy the middle of the back rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Traders who buy from producers and sell on stand between the two parties, hence the name for intermediaries.

clue.text: Sign up as submariner

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an omen is a sign or portent

explanation.surface: A portent is posted, perhaps as a recruitment notice for a submarine crew.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Nemo commands the submarine Nautilus in Jules Verne's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Verne's captain lives aboard his underwater vessel, so he is the classic fictional undersea sailor.

clue.text: Leading by a point, outmanoeuvre other player

parts.note: a team that is up is ahead or leading
a stage is a point in a process, as in at this stage

explanation.surface: A sportsman who is ahead by one point tries to outwit an opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other player' points to the theatre: an actor who moves upstage forces a fellow actor to turn away from the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing attention from a fellow actor, originally by standing further back on stage, is outdoing a co-performer.

clue.text: Possible deputy being examined

definitions.meaning: an actor who learns a part in order to stand in for the lead if needed
split as two words, ... means being looked into

explanation.definitionFit: A stand-in performer is a potential replacement, and something under study is undergoing examination.

clue.text: Clean scrap

definitions.meaning: to clean by rubbing hard with a brush
to scrap a plan is to cancel or drop it

explanation.definitionFit: Scouring hard washes a surface, and informally calling off a plan has the same verb.

clue.text: Merchant threatened with fatal loss of 20

definitions.text: Merchant threatened with fatal loss of 20

parts.words: Merchant threatened with fatal loss of 20
parts.note: the entry at 20 across is the weight of flesh Shylock demands as forfeit in Shakespeare's play set in Venice

explanation.surface: A trader faces deadly ruin over a debt.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Merchant of Venice is named for this character, whose bond lets Shylock cut out a pound of his flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of Shakespeare's Venetian comedy borrows from Shylock against a forfeit of his own flesh.

clue.text: Relaxation many found under canvas

parts.note: ease is relaxation or rest
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: Lots of people find rest in a tent on a camping holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under canvas' suggests camping, but the canvas is a painting propped on its stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter's wooden frame holds the stretched picture, so it sits beneath the work being painted.

clue.text: One in central position editor annoyed

annotationWithheld.why: One in central position editor annoyed: RILED needs I between R and L (right and left) + ED, but no clue word gives R and L except 'central position', which would be both the container indicator and the letters
annotationWithheld.clue: One in central position editor annoyed

clue.text: Put a Russian order back for 3?

indicators.note: back means the pieces are read in reverse, from end to start

parts.note: to set something down is to put it
red was the colour of Soviet Russia, a Red being a communist
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to reverse a Russian command for the third time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses SET A RED OM as a whole. 3 is MIDDLEMEN: political moderates are the people in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Politicians of the centre hold positions between the extremes, so they are men in the middle.

clue.text: Man of the church

parts.note: William ... and his father Frederick were both Archbishops of Canterbury, also a word for a place of worship

explanation.surface: A simple description of a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: The surname of two Archbishops of Canterbury is also a building for worship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Temple family supplied two heads of the Church of England in the twentieth century.

clue.text: Point rebutted in trial court

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other
re-butted: butted back, so the word for point turns round

parts.note: the nub is the central point of an argument

explanation.surface: A lawyer's point is refuted during a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebutted' looks like legal language for refuted, but it is read as butted back, a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel set up to judge disputes is a kind of court of law.

clue.text: No promises broken in academic trip

indicators.note: something broken has its parts out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A college field trip goes ahead without any guarantees being kept.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reverend William Spooner, an Oxford don, was famed for slips of the tongue that swapped first sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A verbal slip named after an Oxford don is literally a scholar's stumble of the tongue.

clue.text: One in a thousand — in a thousand, note

indicators.note: the second in places what comes before inside the pair of thousands

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A rare musical note, one in a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: IN and I go between two Ms, the Roman thousands.
explanation.definitionFit: A half note in music, held for two beats, is called by this old name in British usage.

clue.text: The course is a piece of cake for small French crew

parts.note: petit is French for small
a four is a rowing crew of four oarsmen

explanation.surface: Someone says a dessert course was easy, being served to a small French rowing team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of cake' reads as easy, but it means a little cake.
explanation.definitionFit: These tiny fancy cakes are served with coffee at the end of a meal.

clue.text: Distant part of Ireland, if you go by air

definitions.text: Distant part of Ireland, if you go by air

parts.words: Distant part of Ireland, if you go by air
parts.note: the wartime song says it is a long way to this Irish county, which by air is not so far

explanation.surface: A remote Irish region, reached by plane.
explanation.walkthrough: The First World War marching song 'It's a Long Way to ...' names this county in southern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The song made this Irish county a byword for a far-off place, though by air it is close.

clue.text: Colourful handler of type needed for this dog

parts.note: red is a colour, so it stands for colourful
a typesetter arranges printing type

explanation.surface: A printer with a flair for colour is needed to look after a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The Irish setter, a gundog with a glossy chestnut coat, is often called this.
explanation.definitionFit: This breed of gundog takes its name from its chestnut coat and its habit of crouching at game.

clue.text: Outlaw to commit under-cover offence?

parts.note: split into three words, the name says to steal while wearing a cowl

explanation.surface: A bandit is charged with a crime done in disguise.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as ROB IN HOOD, the name says to steal while hooded.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary English bandit of Sherwood Forest robbed the rich to give to the poor.

clue.text: Shield Queen after club, perhaps, catches King

indicators.note: after places the queen's letters behind the rest
to catch is to grab hold, so one piece is held inside the other
perhaps hints the word club may be taken in another form, its letters reordered

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A queen's guard, following a man with a club, captures a king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' makes a new arrangement of the club's letters; 'catches' puts the king inside, and 'after' sets the Queen's letters at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: This small round shield was held in the hand by medieval foot soldiers.

clue.text: Poet could have enlisted twenty once

definitions.meaning: before decimal coinage, twenty shillings made this unit of British money

explanation.surface: A poet might have joined the army at the age of twenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could have enlisted' is surface only; the old British unit of money was twenty shillings.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra was a modernist poet, and the British currency unit equalled twenty shillings before 1971.

clue.text: U or non-U newcomer?

parts.note: U meant upper-class in 1950s British slang, so a newcomer starting at the top is a social climber

explanation.surface: A new arrival whose social class is uncertain.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U were labels for upper-class and middle-class speech in 1950s Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has risen suddenly in status is seen as a pushy newcomer to high society.

clue.text: Angel, perhaps, blown by the wind

definitions.meaning: the recording angel notes down each person's deeds
a wooden flute played in the woodwind section

explanation.definitionFit: The angel keeping heavenly records takes notes, and a simple flute is a woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Bad specimen sometimes seen in gallery

definitions.meaning: a plant or animal varying from the type, often inferior
a police photo collection of criminals is called a gallery of these

explanation.definitionFit: A wayward individual differs from the norm, and police keep a gallery of photos of criminals.

clue.text: Brought down to ground level — or up, do we hear?

indicators.note: a question about hearing suggests a word that is said the same way

parts.note: raised means lifted up

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a building was demolished or put up.
explanation.walkthrough: RASED is a variant spelling of razed, sounding like raised.
explanation.definitionFit: To raze a building is to flatten it completely, levelling it with the earth.

clue.text: This tenant's left without any quarters

parts.note: the compass quarters east, south, south, east, east, any points of the compass being allowed

explanation.surface: A renter moves out leaving the property without any rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without any' is linking here; quarters are compass points, so any run of E, S, N and W may be used, here five of them.
explanation.definitionFit: A person holding a property under a lease is a renter.

clue.text: Measures of resistance in Royalist cause

definitions.meaning: the letters On His Majesty's Service, printed on official mail

explanation.definitionFit: Units of electrical resistance are named after Georg Ohm, and official mail bore the letters On His Majesty's Service.

clue.text: For writer, material he works with is precious

definitions.meaning: Oliver, the Irish author of The Vicar of Wakefield

definitions.text: material he works with is precious
definitions.meaning: a craftsman who works in gold, a precious metal

explanation.definitionFit: Oliver was an eighteenth-century Irish author, and a craftsman in gold works with precious metal.

clue.text: Stop a huge girl gaining weight — more than one answer

parts.note: Ava is a girl's name
st is the abbreviation for stone, a British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A large girl is told to stop putting on weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gaining' is a linking word; 'more than one answer' admits the alternative A VAST, from 'a huge'.
explanation.definitionFit: This nautical command tells sailors to cease what they are doing.

clue.text: What could make me a lord?

definitions.text: What could make me a lord?

indicators.note: asks what the following letters could be made into, a cue for rearranging them

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how they might gain a peerage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What could make' rearranges ME A LORD; and being granted the title would indeed make one a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank and territory of a peer of the realm confers a noble title.

clue.text: Crooked US lawyer helps to create mass hysteria

indicators.note: the letters run across these words, so they help make it

explanation.surface: A dishonest American attorney stirs up public panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helps to create' means the answer is spelt out inside 'mass hysteria'.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang for an unscrupulous attorney who uses shady methods.
